text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Skopje press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- Macedonian Parliament adopted law on compensation for savers of failed TAT savings scheme. Deputies from Bitola walked out of parliament in disgust over rejection of their amendments.
- Construction began of Kozjak hydro-electric power plant, with 120-metre dam and total cost of $50 milion.

- Presidency of the ethnic-Albanian PDP party to discuss on Friday if party will remain in ruling coalition. Political sources say the ethnic Albanian ministers signed (sealed) letters of resignation months ago.

- Foreign Minister Blagoj Handziski says Macedonia was not rejected by EU, whose resolution refers only to states with associate-member status. Several states in this region were awarded such a status for political reasons at a time the criteria were not particularly strict, he says.
- Macedonian Defence Minister Lazar Kitanovski and his Russian counterpart Ivan Sergeev expected to sign in Moscow on Friday a defence cooperation agreement.
- Macedonian ambassador in Greece denies claim by Greek daily that a deal has been struck for the new name of Macedonia to be 'Republic of Macedonia-Skopje'.
- Macedonian and Yugoslav high-level officials meet, say there is no reason why successful bilateral economic ties should be impossible.
- Well-known Yugoslav Albanian dissident Azem Vllasi visits Macedonia, meets top officials of ethnic-Albanian PDP party.
- British Prime Minister Tony Blair says in message to Macedonian President Kiro Gligorov that Britain supports Macedonia's efforts to gain entrance into North Atlantic structures.
- Government spokesman Zoran Ivanov says there exist no legal grounds for imposing direct rule in the ethnically-troubled municipality of Gostivar.

- Government minister Vlado Naumovski says law on religious organisations designed in complaince with contemporary democratic concepts, ensuring separation of the church from the state, but some churches have asked the constitutional court to determine its legality.

- Owners of private radio and TV stations say the composition of the new Radiodiffusion Council makes it a political body rather than an independent one. -- Mircela Casule, Skopje newsroom +389 91 201 196
